result.topic_en: Euler shows that the prime factors of residues are themselves residues. He conjectures that all prime factors of numbers n−q²−q and q²+q−n occur among the residues, and tests this with tables of the numbers p and the simple residues r for 4n+1 = 5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 41, 53, 61.
result.transcription:
quam producta ex binis pluribusue, pariter in residuis occurrere debeant; vnde patet, si iam prodierint residua $\alpha\gamma$ et $\beta\gamma$, tum etiam residuum fore $\alpha\beta$. Quia enim productum $\alpha\beta\gamma\gamma$ est residuum, omisso quadrato $\gamma\gamma$ etiam $\alpha\beta$ erit residuum.

Corollarium 3.

§. 12. Quodsi ergo compertum fuerit residuum $\alpha\beta$, ex alio autem casu residuum prodeat $\alpha$, etiam alter factor $\beta$ erit residuum.

Scholion.

§. 13. Cum huiusmodi combinationes binorum residuorum pluribus, immo infinitis modis institui queant, hinc iam maxime verisimile videtur, praeter ipsos numeros in formulis $n-qq-q$ et $qq+q-n$ contentos etiam omnes eorum factores primos in residuis occurrere, quae coniectura vtrum fundamento certo innitatur nec ne, per sequentia exempla exploremus. Hunc in finem exponamus numeros in formula $qq+q$ contentos, qui sunt
$0, 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, 56, 72, 90, 110, 132, 156,$
$182, 210, 240, 272, 306, 342, 380, 420,$ etc.
et quemadmodum residua hinc nata littera $p$ designamus, ita residua prima seu simplicia littera $r$ indicemus, et quo facilius perspiciatur, omnes factores numerorum $p$ quoque esse residua, ipsos numeros $p$ per suos factores primos repraesentemus:
1°. Sit $4n+1=5$; erit $n=1$.
$p=1, 1, 5, 11, 19, 29, 41, 5\cdot 11, 71,$ etc.
$r=1, 5, 11, 19, 29, 41, 71,$ etc.
vbi

[p. 273]
vbi patet, numeri compositi $p$, qui est vnicus $5\cdot 11$, ipsos factores quoque esse residua.
2°. Sit $4n+1=13$; $n=3$.
$p=3, 1, 3, 3^2, 3^3, 3\cdot 13, 53, 3\cdot 23,$ etc.
$r=1, 3, 13, 23, 53,$ etc.
3°. Sit $4n+1=17$; $n=4$.
$p=2^2, 2, 2, 2^3, 2^4, 2\cdot 13, 2\cdot 19, 2^2\cdot 13, 2^2\cdot 17, 2\cdot 43$ etc.
$r=1, 2, 13, 17, 19\ 43,$ etc.
4°. Sit $4n+1=29$; $n=7$.
$p=7, 5, 1, 5, 13, 23, 5\cdot 7, 7^2, 5\cdot 13, 83, 103,$ etc.
$r=1, 5, 7, 13, 23, 83, 103,$ etc.
5°. Sit $4n+1=37$; $n=9$.
$p=3^2, 7, 3, 3, 11, 19, 3\cdot 11, 43, 59, 7\cdot 11, 101,$ etc.
$r=1, 3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 59, 101,$ etc.
6°. Sit $4n+1=41$; $n=10$.
$p=2\cdot 5, 2^3, 2^2, 2, 2\cdot 5, 2^2\cdot 5, 2^5, 2\cdot 23, 2\cdot 31, 2^4\cdot 5,$
$2^2\cdot 5^2,$ etc.
$r=1, 2, 5, 23, 31,$ etc.
vbi patet, in numeris $p$ nullos factores primos conspici, qui non simul sint residua.
7°. Sit $4n+1=53$; $n=13$.
$p=13, 11, 7, 1, 7, 17, 29, 43, 59, 7\cdot 11, 97,$ etc.
$r=1, 7, 11, 13, 17, 29, 43, 59, 97,$ etc.
8°. Sit $4n+1=61$; $n=15$.
$p=3\cdot 5, 13, 3^2, 3, 5, 3\cdot 5, 3^3, 41, 3\cdot 19, 3\cdot 5^2, 5\cdot 19$ etc.
$r=1, 3, 5, 13, 19, 41,$ etc.
Euleri Opusc. Anal. Tom. I.  Mm  9°.

items.quote: si iam prodierint residua $\alpha\gamma$ et $\beta\gamma$, tum etiam residuum fore $\alpha\beta$.
items.english: If the residues αγ and βγ have already appeared, then αβ will also be a residue.

items.quote: Quodsi ergo compertum fuerit residuum $\alpha\beta$, ex alio autem casu residuum prodeat $\alpha$, etiam alter factor $\beta$ erit residuum.
items.english: If αβ has been found to be a residue, and from another case α arises as a residue, then the other factor β will also be a residue.

items.quote: praeter ipsos numeros in formulis $n-qq-q$ et $qq+q-n$ contentos etiam omnes eorum factores primos in residuis occurrere, quae coniectura vtrum fundamento certo innitatur nec ne, per sequentia exempla exploremus.
items.english: Besides the numbers contained in the formulas n−q²−q and q²+q−n themselves, all their prime factors also occur among the residues. Let us explore by the following examples whether this conjecture rests on a sure foundation or not.
